judged_text: createEvent receives destination.externalId but forwards only credential.id to calendar.createEvent, forcing every service to re-derive its target calendar (Google via a credentialId scan, the others incorrectly via [0]) even though the resolved externalId was already in hand at the call site. The target-calendar policy is duplicated per service instead of resolved once by the manager; forwarding externalId (which is already threaded into the result) would let Lark/O365/Base delete their broken [0] fallbacks and make the new credentialId parameter unnecessary — the next provider added to the app store will repeat the same mistake.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` iterating over `event.destinationCalendar` and calling `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` for each destination, but `CalendarManager.createEvent` ignores the `externalId` argument when calling the provider (`calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`). As a result, providers must infer the target calendar from `calEvent.destinationCalendar`. Google does this via `find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, but Lark/O365/BaseCalendarService now use `[0]` (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and therefore will always target the first destination calendar even when creating events for subsequent destinations in the loop, causing events to be created in the wrong calendar.
